enonce_markdown: The Truman Doctrine of March 1947 first offered American aid to:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Place the doctrine in its immediate crisis: where was a communist advance feared in early 1947?

### Solution

President Truman asked Congress for aid to Greece, where communist guerrillas were fighting the government, and to Turkey, under Soviet pressure. The Marshall Plan, which came later in 1947-48, concerned the economic recovery of Western Europe in general.

enonce_markdown: Name the American diplomat who first set out the idea of containment and the document through which it became public in 1947, then state what he advised.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Name the author, the text, the date and the central advice.

### Solution

George Kennan, who had sent the 'Long Telegram' from Moscow in 1946, published the 'X' article in the journal Foreign Affairs in 1947. He advised a long-term, patient but firm and vigilant policy of containing Soviet expansion, by applying counter-pressure at points where the USSR tried to extend its influence.

enonce_markdown: The Marshall Plan (1948-1952) is considered part of the policy of containment because it:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Containment was not only military. Ask what condition the plan was meant to remove.

### Solution

General Marshall's plan gave about thirteen billion dollars in economic aid to the countries of Western Europe. Its aim was to rebuild economies, reduce poverty and unemployment and so deprive communist parties of the discontent on which they fed. It was an economic, not a military, measure, it did not punish the USSR, and it did not aim at reuniting Germany.

choix.texte: created a military alliance against the USSR
rebuilt Western European economies and so removed the conditions in which communism could win support
imposed economic sanctions on the Soviet Union and its allies
set up a plan to reunite Germany under a neutral government

enonce_markdown: During the Berlin Blockade (June 1948 - May 1949) the Western response of the Berlin Airlift illustrates containment because it:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Containment meant resisting Soviet pressure without starting a direct war. Look for the response which holds the line while avoiding the first shot.

### Solution

Stalin closed the land routes to West Berlin. The Western powers did not send an armoured convoy, which might have started a war; they supplied the city by air for almost a year, until the blockade was lifted. The West neither gave up Berlin nor used force first.

choix.texte: abandoned Berlin to avoid war with the USSR
forced open the land routes with armoured convoys
kept West Berlin free from Soviet control without direct armed confrontation
replaced the blockade by an atomic attack on Soviet forces

enonce_markdown: Explain why the creation of NATO in 1949 can be seen as an application of the policy of containment.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Say what the organisation was, what it promised, and whom it was meant to deter.

### Solution

NATO was a military alliance of the USA, Canada and ten Western European states signed in April 1949. Its Article 5 stated that an armed attack against one member would be treated as an attack on all, which tied the United States permanently to the defence of Western Europe. It was meant to deter Soviet attack or pressure after events such as the Czechoslovak coup (1948) and the Berlin Blockade, and so to stop communism from spreading westwards. The USSR answered with the Warsaw Pact in 1955.

enonce_markdown: A common criticism of the way containment was applied in Asia, for example in Vietnam, is that it:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Evaluate a policy by asking what assumption it made. Check which option names a real weakness of the assumption.

### Solution

Critics argued that American leaders treated national movements such as Ho Chi Minh's as pieces of a single worldwide communist bloc directed from Moscow, and so overlooked local nationalism and anti-colonial feeling. The Soviet Union was the main target of the policy, economic aid was only one of its tools, and the policy led to more, not less, American involvement abroad.

choix.texte: treated nationalist movements as part of a single communist bloc and ignored local nationalism
relied only on economic aid and never used military force
ignored the Soviet Union and aimed only at China
led the United States back to isolationism
